links.title: Midwest Filtration Co
links.description: USA. Manufacturers and converters of woven and nonwoven filter media and manufactured filter products for dry and liquid filtration applications. Also, distributors of wet- and dry-laid, spunbond and spunlace nonwovens.

links.title: Confortaire, Inc
links.description: USA. Distributors of polyurethane foam products and polyester nonwovens to the furniture upholstery, healthcare, filtration, automotive, packaging and home craft industries.

links.title: Nowotec Srl
links.description: Italy. Manufacturers' representatives for carded and air-laid, spunbond, meltblown and SMS nonwoven fabrics, and nonwoven composites, from polyester, polypropylene and polyethylene.

links.title: Prato TnT SpA
links.description: Italy. Manufacturers and suppliers of spunlace, spunbond and airthrough nonwoven rolls, and wipes, towlettes, apparel, bags and accessories for hospitality, medical, packaging, agriculture and furnishing applications. Multi-lingual site.

links.title: Alphamin SA
links.description: Belgium. International distributors of speciality polymers and waxes, and polyester nonwovens for bitumen modification applications.

links.title: FilzFelt
links.description: USA. German-milled wool design felt and felt products including acoustic solutions, drapery, floor coverings, hanging panels, and wall panels. Detailed product catalogs, including prices.

links.title: Xamax Industries, Inc
links.description: USA. Distributors of paper products, films, nonwovens, tissues and pressure sensitive tapes to a variety of industries. Needlepunch, spunbond and spunlace fabrics, from polyester, polypropylene, polyamide and high-performance fibers.

282211.title: Organizations
282211.description: This category lists trade and professional associations, related to the textile and nonwovens industries only.

links.title: Quality Mattresses Manufacturers Consortium
links.description: Italy. Non-profit organization of mattress manufacturing companies, dedicated to quality certification, information and technology transfer, and consumer education. List of member companies. English and Italian.

links.title: Textile, Clothing and Footwear Union of Australia
links.description: Official site of the Australian union for employees in the textile, apparel and footwear industries.

links.title: TSA. Textile Society of the Americas
links.description: USA. Association of students from the College of Textiles at North Carolina State University, with the purpose of offering the industry not only bilingual but also knowledgeable professionals of the Latin American culture. List of resumes. Links to related sites. [English and Spanish]

links.title: ANSI. American National Standards Institute
links.description: USA. Federal institute, promoting development and application of standardization in the manufacturing and service industries. Web site offers news, articles, on-line standards store and up to date information about national and international standardization activities.

links.title: ASTM International
links.description: USA. Standards development organization that serves as an open forum for the development of high-quality, market-relevant international standards.

links.title: BISFA. International Bureau for the Standardization of Man-made Fibers
links.description: Belgium. Standardization agency of the International Association of Man-made Fiber Producers. Establishes terminology and technical rules for development, production, handling and marketing of each specific type of fiber.

links.title: NIST. National Institute of Standards and Technology
links.description: USA. Federal agency, cooperating with industry to develop and apply technologies, measurements, and standards.

links.title: ISO. International Organization for Standardization
links.description: Switzerland. World wide federation of national standards institutes, promoting the development of standardization of goods and services. In English and French.

282037.title: Resources
282037.description: This category lists data bases for the textile and nonwovens industries, informational and educational resources for management and professionals, industry publications and electronic magazines.

links.title: BTTG. British Textile Technology Group
links.description: UK. Independent textile and nonwovens research and technology center, also providing services to a range of other spheres of industry and commerce.

links.title: SAMPE. Society for the Advancement of Materials and Process Engineering
links.description: USA. International professional member society, provides information on new materials and process technologies through forums, publications and books.

links.title: SATRA Technology Centre
links.description: UK. Authority on the technical aspects of footwear, leathergoods, apparel, toys, safety products, furniture, floorcoverings, construction products and homeware. Involved in product research and development, material and component evaluation, quality assurance, manufacturing efficiency and cost saving, and testing and certification.

links.title: National Textile Center
links.description: USA. Federally funded consortium of universities, dedicated to applied research on fibers, textiles and related subjects. Searchable database of past and present research projects.

links.title: Saxon Textile Research Institute
links.description: Germany. Application oriented research and development projects for the textile and nonwovens industries. Also,  laboratory testing and certification services. English and German.

links.title: IPFDD. Institute for Polymer Research Dresden
links.description: Germany. Public institute for application oriented fundamental research in polymer architecture, interaction mechanisms, and fundamental materials. Activities in fiber reinforced composites, modified polymer membranes, and meltspun nonwovens. List of lectures and conferences. Links to related sites.

links.title: TUT - Institute of Fiber Material Science
links.description: Finland. Research and development institute of the Tampere University of Technology, specialising in fiber technology and textile chemistry, textile and nonwovens technologies, and electro-conductive fabrics and wearables. English and Finnish.

links.title: Textile Research Institute
links.description: Poland. Independent institute for research, development, testing and certification in the fiber, yarn, textile and nonwovens industries. English and Polish.

links.title: Textile World
links.description: Search engine for manufacturers of fibers, yarns, greige and finished woven and knitted fabrics, apparel, bedding, trimmings, closeouts, transportation and textile machinery. English and Italian.

links.title: BIR. Bureau of International Recycling
links.description: Belgium. International trade federation for the recycling industry, focused on ferrous and non-ferrous metals, paper, textiles, plastics and rubber.

links.title: ITCF. Institute for Textile Chemistry and Chemical Fibers Denkendorf
links.description: Germany. Government funded institute for fundamental and applied research, and technology transfer in the field of fibers and textiles with regard to manufacturing, modification, characterization and processing. English and German.

links.title: DVS. German Welding Society
links.description: Non-profit technical and scientific society for individuals and companies, involved in research and education on matters relating to the joining, cutting and coating of metallic and non-metallic materials, composite materials and technical textiles and nonwovens, and publishing  journals, specialist books, research reports, software, guidelines and codes of practice oriented to science and practice. English and German.

links.title: ITA. Institut für Textiltechnik
links.description: Germany. Competence center and research institute for man-made fiber, nonwovens and textile technology, and mechanical engineering. Links to related sites. Multi-lingual site.

links.title: World Textile Information Network
links.description: Information resource providing industry news and analysis about the yarn spinning, textile and nonwovens industries. Requires subscription. Published by World Textile Publications, Ltd.

links.title: International Textile Center
links.description: USA. Non-profit organization of the Texas Tech University, dedicated to applied research, testing and evaluation of textile fabrics, fibers and processes. Extensive library of articles on cotton growing and processing.

282054.title: Articles and Studies
282054.description: This category will only contain links to the various categories in Textiles and Nonwovens in which educational and research information, articles, and technical papers and reports are listed, and serves as a quick entrance point to that information.

282055.title: Filtration
282055.description: This category contains links only to sub-categories in Textiles and Nonwovens, listing scientific articles and studies related to filtration technology.

links.title: New Polypropylene Media for String-Wound Filter Cartridges
links.description: Technical paper presenting a new string-wound filter cartridge with friction spun polypropylene yarns for the reduction of sediments and suspended impurities in water and liquids, with a random winding structure which prevents media migration and chemical leaching. From Syntech Fibres Pvt., Ltd. Author: Hamid Omar.

282048.title: Composite Materials
282048.description: This category lists information resources for the composite industry only.

links.title: Worldwide Composites Search Engine
links.description: Search engine for advanced composite materials, honeycombs, prepegs, film adhesives, fabrics and related industry services and products. Also featuring surplus material sales, and key personnel listings.

links.title: FiberglassBlog
links.description: Andy Keson's blog providing information and resources related to composites materials.

links.title: Composite Materials
links.description: Short article on the different reinforcement structures in the composite industry, and descriptions of the most common polymeric and inorganic fibers in use. From the New Textiles magazine.

links.title: Interfacial Structure and Properties of Wood/Polypropylene Composites
links.description: Technical paper about the development of thermoplastic composites utilizing lignocellulosic, low quality hardwood fiber as reinforcing component. Authors: Timothy G. Rials and others.

links.title: Draping of Woven Composites over Irregular Surfaces
links.description: Technical paper about research aimed at providing a basis for the development of a drape model, based on the properties of the woven fabric and the mold shape. Authors: S.B. Sharma and M.P.F. Sutcliffe.

links.title: Automated Fabrication Technologies for High-Performance Polymer Composites
links.description: Extensive technical paper reviewing new automated fabrication processes for the manufacture of high-performance graphite-fiber reinforced composite structures. Authors: M.J. Stuart and others.

links.title: An Overview of Composite Actuators with Piezoceramic Fiber
links.description: Technical paper discussing the manufacturing processes, intended applications and relative benefits of four different types of active fiber composite actuators. Authors: R. Brett Williams and Daniel J. Inman.

links.title: Natural Fibre Composites in Structural Components: Alternative Applications for Sisal?
links.description: Technical article about the processing techniques and applications of bast, leaf and seed fibers in the composite industry. Author: W.D. Brouwer.

links.title: Properties of Biocomposites Based on Ligno Cellulosic Fillers
links.description: Scientific paper analysing the thermal and mechanical behaviour of processed biocomposites, created by extrusion and injection molding a matrix of aromatic co-polyesters and ligno-cellulosic filler material. Authors: L. Averous and F. Le Digabel.

282049.title: Research
282049.description: This category lists private and public institutions and companies, involved in research and development activities for the composite industry.

links.title: American Carbon Society
links.description: USA. Based at Pennsylvania State University, the American Carbon Society promotes interdisciplinary research and technology in the field of carbon science.

links.title: CCM. Center for Composite Materials
links.description: USA. Engineering, research and educational center for composites science and technology, based in the University of Delaware. Interactive learning tools. Lists of current and completed projects, and publications and technical reports. Job opportunities.

links.title: Institut für Verbundwerkstoffe GmbH
links.description: Germany. Non-profit research institute involved in the investigation and development of technical applications and applicabilities of composite materials. Also active in knowledge transfer and education. English and German.

links.title: Institute of Plastics Engineering
links.description: Germany. Non-profit, industrial research organization, dedicated to applied research, education and training in plastics technologies and processing. Its Fiber Composites Department is active in process engineering and development for practical applications.

links.title: Sicomp AB
links.description: Sweden. Research and technology institute for fibrous, composite and polymer materials. Also, testing and consulting services. Searchable publications directory. Article archive. List of member and partner companies. Links to related sites. Part of the Swerea Group. English and Swedish.

links.title: TITK. Thüringer Institute for Textile and Plastics Research
links.description: Germany. Fundamental and applied research and product development in structural and functional polymers, fiber reinforced composites and recycling processes. Detailed descriptions of ongoing projects. List of publications. English and German.

links.title: Bangor University
links.description: UK. The Bio-composites Centre. Research department, specialising in industrial contract research on the processing of wood and plant materials.

links.title: British Composites Society
links.description: UK. Composites division in the Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining of the University of London, dedicated to education and research. Introduction to composites. List of publications. Calendar of events. Links to standards information and composite related sites.

282051.title: Dictionaries
282051.description: This category lists on-line lists of acronyms, dictionaries, definitions and glossaries of terms which are related to the textile, apparel and nonwovens industries only.

links.title: Waterjet Glossary
links.description: Glossary of waterjet and abrasivejet related terms. From Carl Olson's web site.

links.title: Trade Terms Dictionary
links.description: A dictionary of general trade terms and definitions. From the Bureau of Export Administration.

links.title: Glossary of Toxic Terms
links.description: Glossary of technical terms used in environmental health publications. From the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry.

links.title: Rope Glossary
links.description: Glossary of technical terms in the rope manufacturing industry.

links.title: Nanotechnology Glossary
links.description: Glossary of nanotechnology and nanoscale science and technology terms. From the Nanotechnology Now e-zine.

links.title: Tradenames for Plastics
links.description: A glossary of trade names in the plastics industry, including short material descriptions and company origin.

links.title: Starch and Glucose Glossary
links.description: Glossary on starch, glucose syrup and starch hydrolysates.

links.title: Glossary of Coating Terms
links.description: A glossary of technical terms and definitions used in the polymer coating industry. From Whitford Corp.

282038.title: History
282038.description: This category lists web sites on the history of textiles, the industry, technologies and materials.

links.title: Color Museum
links.description: Information resource on color order systems in art and science. Illustrated color theories from Antiquity to modern times. The significance of colors in cultural systems. Interactive journey through Philip Otto Runge's color sphere. Chronological bibliography. English, German and French.

links.title: Museum of Fiber Science and Technology
links.description: Japan. Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology museum exhibition of historic collections of data, materials, equipment and machinery related to silk cultivation and processing, and natural and man-made fiber development and production. English and Japanese.

links.title: Wallpaper History Society
links.description: UK. Registered charity established to promote the international awareness and understanding of historic and contemporary wallcoverings, encouraging research and providing information on all aspects of wallpaper history, design, production, manufacture and consumption.

links.title: Arkwright, Richard
links.description: Biography of the inventor of the industrial cotton spinning mill. Links to illustrations and local history. 1732-1792.

links.title: Paul, Lewis
links.description: Short history of the inventor of a hand driven carding machine for cotton fiber processing.

links.title: Jacquard, Joseph
links.description: Short history of the inventor of a loom which produced repeated weave patterns in cloth and carpets, programmed by a series of punched cards. 1752-1834.

282042.title: Hargreaves, James
282042.description: Inventor of the yarn spinning jenny.

links.title: Hargreaves, James
links.description: Biography of the British carpenter, weaver and self-made engineer who invented the eight-thread spinning jenny. 1720-1778.

282040.title: Kay, John
282040.description: Patented the flying shuttle in 1733.  Born: 1704 Died: 1780

links.title: Mr.John Kay
links.description: Extract from a facsimile of Debow's review.

links.title: John Kay
links.description: A short biography with related links and a section of a mural produced by William Bell Scott . From Spartacus Educational .

links.title: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
links.description: Description, historic development and current situation of sweatshops, of which those related to the textile industry are the most notorious. Links to related sites. Authors: Peter Liebhold and Harry Rubenstein.

links.title: From Weaver to Web
links.description: Project undertaken by the UK Calderdale Council aimed at raising the historic profile of the Calderdale area, one of its key elements being the development of a searchable visual archive featuring material relating to the textile industry that grew, rose to fame and eventually declined in and around the Halifax area.

links.title: A Global History of Textile Workers, 1650-2000
links.description: Project of the International Institute of Social History, dedicated to the creation of a global and comparative history of textile workers 1650-2000. Links to national overviews and comparative papers on Word files.

links.title: History of Textile Business in North Carolina
links.description: History of North Carolina's web site about the development of the cotton textile industry of the state, from 1810 to the present day with links to historical mills and laureates.

links.title: Knitting Together
links.description: Joint Internet project of the Leicester City Museum Service and its partners, dedicated to the history of the East-Midlands knitting industry. Timeline. Oral and photographic history. Virtual museum. Resources and links.

links.title: River Wey & Navigations
links.description: Extensive information about the leather and wool processing, yarn spinning, weaving and textile manufacturing industry in the Wey Valley in the United Kingdom since the 13th Century.

links.title: Cotton Town
links.description: The story of the rapid social and economic changes that occurred as Blackburn and Darwen began to expand in line with the United Kingdom textile industry, providing collection of material, based on the influence of the cotton trade.

links.title: The Textile System
links.description: A collection of articles on inventions, inventors and entrepreneurs in the British textile industry of the 18th and 19th centuries. Also, descriptions of the conditions in textile mills, factory workers and child labor. From Spartacus Schoolnet.

links.title: The Textile Heritage Museum
links.description: Ongoing restoration project as well as a museum highlighting the textile history of Alamance County and the Piedmont, USA, featuring the history and machinery of the textile industry from the cottage industry to the present, the family labor system, life in the mill villages, and a company store exhibit.

links.title: River Powers Textile Industry
links.description: Short history of the development of the cotton textile industry in Lowell, Massachusetts, from 1826 to its peak as a major textile center in 1924. From the Cities of the United States web site.

links.title: The Chronology of Textiles and Fiber Arts in New Mexico
links.description: Timeline of the history and development of weaving techniques and the textile industry in New Mexico, from 700 BC until the present. From The Collector's Guide web site.

links.title: Verdant Works
links.description: The history of the jute industry in Dundee, Scotland, from 1833 when the first jute textile mill was built by merchant and flax spinner David Lindsay, until the industry's decline in the 1960's.

links.title: The Life of a Weaver in the Early 19th Century
links.description: Extract from an article in the Stroud Journal, published in 1868, telling the story of textile workers and working conditions around the time of the Stroudwater Riots of 1825. Includes the poem 'A Weaving Factory' by Thomas Delaney.

links.title: Photographs of Milltowns in England, Great Britain and India.
links.description: On-line exhibition of large format photographs of textile mills in New England, USA, Britain and India, from Randolph Langenbach's collection.

links.title: No Idle Hands, The Social History of American Knitting
links.description: Review of a textbook about the history of home and industrial machine knitting in the United States from Independence until the present time. Author: Anne L. Macdonald.

links.title: Weaving in Yorkshire
links.description: Illustrated history of the cloth weaving industry in the Yorkshire area of the United Kingdom in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

links.title: The Woollen Industry
links.description: Extract of a book written in 1935 for the London Carmarthenshire Society, providing a brief history of the woollen industry in Carmarthenshire, Wales, Great Britain, which' first records date back to the Norman occupation and virtually disappeared at the start of the 20th century.

links.title: The Woollen Industry in Medieval Clare
links.description: The history of the woollen cloth and quilt making industry in Clare, Sufflok County, Great Britain, which probably dates back to the 11th century and saw its peak in the 16th century. From 'A Short History of Clare, Suffolk' by Gladys A. Thornton.

links.title: Lowell National Historical Park
links.description: The history of Lowell's planned textile mill city, founded during the second quarter of the 1800's, which in scale, technological innovation, and development of an urban working class, marked the beginning of the industrial transformation of America.

links.title: Textile Production in Europe, 1600–1800
links.description: Introduction to silk weaving, lace making, tapestry, embroidery and printing as the principal European textile industries between 1600 and 1800. Compiled by Melinda Watt. From the web site of The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

links.title: History of Knitting
links.description: The history of knitting, from the early nålebinding technique involving the creation of fabric from thread by making multiple knots or loops, to the current high-speed circular and flat bed knitting technologies. Author: Julie Theaker.

links.title: The Woollen Industry of Moreton
links.description: History of the woollen industry and its organization in Moreton, Devon, Great Britain, which' existence was first recorded in 1297.

282044.title: Articles and Studies
282044.description: This category contains links to articles, scientific papers, studies and lectures related to the history of the textile and allied industries.

links.title: A History of Cotton Mills and the Industrial Revolution
links.description: Extensive excerpt of a book on the development of the textile industry in Mississippi, USA. Author: Narvell Strickland.

links.title: Australian Innovation in Textile Technology
links.description: A review of the history, development and current state of the art in textile technologies and processes. From the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering's Technology in Australia 1788-1988.

links.title: Mill Life in Lowell: 1820-1880
links.description: Collection of essays, photographs, images, letters and songs related to the daily life of cotton textile workers on Lowell, Massachusetts, during a period that lasted nearly a century. From the Center for Lowell History.

links.title: Child Labor and the Division of Labor in the Early English Cotton Mills
links.description: Pre-publication draft paper from 1994 about child labor in the English cotton textile industry, the move away from it prior to child labor legislation in the early 1830's, and the development of a labor market for productive adult factory workers during the Industrial Revolution. Author: Douglas A. Galbi.

links.title: Economic Change and Sex Discrimination in the Early English Cotton Factories
links.description: Research paper discussing the wage discrimination between men and women working in the early English cotton textile industry, using a labor sorting model as an alternative explanation of how discrimination could be transmitted from established labor markets to the new factory labor market. Author: Douglas A. Galbi.

links.title: The Relocation of the Market for Australian Wool, 1880-1939
links.description: Working paper analysing the historical developments which caused the international wool auction market to shift decisively from Britain to Australia during the period between 1880 and the start of the Second World War. Author: Simon Ville.

links.title: Gold, Guilds and Government
links.description: Extensive paper about the impact of monetary and labor policies on the Flemish cloth industry, dealing with the period between 1390 and 1435. Author: Prof. John H. Munro.

links.title: The Symbiosis of Towns and Textiles
links.description: Discussion paper examining the relative advantages of urban and rural locations for cloth manufacturing in later Medieval England and the Low Countries in the period between 1270 and 1570. Author: Prof. John H. Munro.

links.title: A Global History of Ottoman Cotton Textiles, 1600-1850
links.description: European University Institute 2007 working paper, revisiting and situating the historiography of Ottoman cotton textiles within ongoing debates concerning the emergence of a world economy through the lens of the cotton industry as the first global industry. Author: Athanasios Gekas.

links.title: The Philosophy of the Manufacturers
links.description: Article written by Prof. Andrew Ure in 1835, enthusiastically promoting the development of mechanised textile manufacturing in the factory system invented during the Industrial Revolution. From the Modern History Sourcebook.

links.title: Industry Structure and the Marketing of Synthetic Fibers
links.description: Paper published in 1990 by the Business History Conference about the explosive growth of organic chemicals and synthetic polymers since World War II, resulting in a move away from using natural fibers in favor of man-made fibers. Author: Amy L. Hardin.

links.title: The Impact of Monetary and Labour Policies on the Flemish Cloth Industry
links.description: Study focusing on the consequences of monetary policy in aggravating ongoing conflict in the English and Dutch cloth industry's labor relations during the late 14th Century. Author: John Munro. Text abstract. Full article on PDF document.

links.title: The Low Countries' Export Trade in Textiles with the Mediterranean Basin
links.description: Cost-benefit analysis, challenging the conventional wisdom in European economic history that long-distance maritime transport in 1200-1600 as always more cost effective than overland trade routes. Author: John H. Munro. Text abstract. Full article on PDF document.

links.title: The "Industrial Crisis" of the English Textile Towns
links.description: Working paper arguing that the industrial crisis of the traditional English textile towns during the period 1290-1340 was caused by a far reaching economic crisis afflicting their major cloth markets in the Mediterranean basin, rather then the emergence of supposedly superior, lower-cost rural competition. Author: John H. Munro. Text abstract. Full text on PDF document.

links.title: Industrial Change in the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Century Low Countries
links.description: Review of the circumstances which resulted in Merino wools to become the chief woollen cloth in the southern Low Countries during the later fifteenth and early sixteenth Century. Author: John H. Munro. Text abstract. Full article on PDF document.

links.title: Textiles as Articles of Consumption in Flemish Towns
links.description: Reconstruction of a Flemish basket of consumables price index for the period 1350-1500, aimed to determine the value of luxury broad woven woollen cloth related to income. Text abstract. Full article on PDF document. Author: John H. Munro.

links.title: The West European Woollen Industries and their Struggles for International Markets
links.description: Working paper presenting a macro- and micro-economic historical study of competition in the West European woollen textile industries, from ca 1000 to 1500. Author: John Munro.

links.title: Cotton Promotes Slavery
links.description: Short article from 'An Outline of American History', showing how the combination of the introduction of new types of cotton, Eli Whitney's invention of the cotton gin and the Industrial Revolution which vastly increased demand for cotton, contributed to the continuation of slavery in the United States.

links.title: Flemish Woollens and German Commerce during the Later Middle Ages
links.description: Article on the major changes in textile products, production costs, prices, and market orientations during the era. Author: John Munro.

links.title: The Symbiosis of Towns and Textiles
links.description: Extensive working paper on the effects of urbanization of the textile industry on cloth manufacturing in the Low Countries and England between 1280 and 1570 CE. Author: John H. Munro. Text abstract, and full text on PDF document.

282045.title: Mills
282045.description: This category contains links to web sites dedicated to historic yarn spinning or cloth weaving mills.

links.title: Charlottesville Woolen Mills
links.description: History of Charlottesville and its cotton textile industry from the 1830's to the first World War. Includes articles about the 1918 strike and the mill workers, historic maps and a blog.

links.title: Coldharbour Mill
links.description: Historic worsted yarn spinning mill which is still in operation, built by Thomas Fox in 1799 in the village of Uffculme, Devon, UK, and active in education, guided tours and workshops. Calendar of events. Links to related sites.

links.title: The Falls of the Clyde, New Lanark Mills
links.description: Description of the 18th century water powered cotton spinning mill built by David Dale and Richard Arkwright, and the village that developed around it.

links.title: Glendale Cotton Mill
links.description: Short article about the history, development and time of prosperity, and eventual decline and closure of the Glendale Cotton Mill at Spartanburg, South Carolina, USA. From the pages of Glendale, South Carolina.

links.title: Whitchurch Silk Mill
links.description: Web site about the Whitchurch textile mill and mill village in Whitchurch, UK, originally built in 1800 as a fulling mill and transformed into a silk weaving mill by William Maddick in 1816. Purchased by the Hampshire Buildings Preservation Trust in 1985 it currently serves as a textile education and preservation center and working museum, producing silk and silk rich fabrics for theatrical costumes, interior designers and historic houses.

links.title: Bemis Mill Village
links.description: Historic cotton mill and mill town in Bemis, Tennessee, constructed in 1900 and listed on the National Registry of Historic Places. Detailed history and stories.

links.title: B.J. Bandy and Bartow Textiles: Creating an Industry
links.description: The history of the Bartow Textiles Company, producers of turfted carpets and bed spreads in Cartersville, Georgia, and the family that created it, which was built in 1940 and developed into one of  the largest tufting companies in the country until its closure in 1953. Author: Randall L. Patton.

links.title: Stanley Mill
links.description: History of the Stanley Mills in Stanley, North Carolina, built in 1891 and in continuous operation as a textile mill under various different owners until its final closure  in the 1980s.

links.title: Langthwaite Cotton Mill
links.description: Part of the article 'Langthwaite Cotton Mill' by D.J.W.Mawson in The Transactions of the Cumberland and Westmorland Antiquarian and Archaeological Society for 1976, presenting the history of the Langthwaite cotton mill in Carlisle, UK, from 1790 to its closure in 1888. From the Industrial History of Cumbria.

links.title: Catherine Street Mill
links.description: The history of the Catherine Street flax mill in Whitehaven, UK, built in 1809 and closed with the decline of the linen industry in 1853. Excerpt from the article 'Who Built the Catherine Street Mill?' by Margaret Robinson.

links.title: Derwent Valley Mills
links.description: Series of silk and cotton textile mills constructed since 1721 in the Derwent Valley area in England, and which from 1770's onwards followed Richard Arkwright's waterpowered factory system model. History and descriptions of mills. Biographies. Glossary of terms. List of publications and bibliography. Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2001.

links.title: Lonaconing Silk Mill
links.description: Project of Allegany High School students Anne Failing, Erin Degyansky, Chris Jewell and Amber Sallerson, researching the history of the Lonaconing silk textile mill in Cumberland, Maryland, which was in operation from 1907 until 1957.

links.title: Chicken Hill
links.description: The history of the Asheville Cotton Mill and the Chicken Hill mill village in Asheville, North Carolina, constructed in the 1880's by the C. E. Graham Manufacturing Company, purchased by the Cone Mills in 1894 which operated it until its final closure in 1953.

links.title: The Cotton Mills of Bombay
links.description: The history of the development of the cotton textile industry and the growth of the number of textile mills in Bombay, India, from the construction of the first cotton mill in 1854 to 70 mills in the wake of the American Civil War in 1895.

links.title: Ballasalla Cotton Mill
links.description: The short lived history of the water powered Ballasalla Cotton Mill on the Isle of Man, UK, founded in 1780 by Deeemster Thomas Moore and folded in 1794 as a result of import duties imposed by and Act of Parliament.

links.title: Greenwood Cotton Mill
links.description: History of one of the oldest and most successful cotton mills in the United States in Greenwood, South Carolina, which was founded in 1889 by William Lowndes Durst and acquired by the Self family in 1935, under which ownership it still operates today as Greenwood Mills, Inc.

links.title: Whittier Cotton Mills
links.description: The history of the Whittier Cotton Mills and mill village in Chattahoochee, Georgia, founded in 1895 by Paul Butler, son of Civil War general Benjamin Butler, and ceased operations in 1971 as a result of cheap textile imports.

links.title: Barrington Woolen Mill
links.description: Web site of the water powered woollen textile mill in Barrington Nova Scotia, Canada, founded in 1882 and closed in 1962 after which it became part of the Nova Scotia museum system.

links.title: Lithgow Woollen Mills
links.description: History of the water and steam powered woollen mills in Lithgow, Australia, founded in 1857 by Andrew Brown to produce tweed, and in continuous operation until the company folded in 1972.

links.title: The History of Neilston Village and its Mill

links.title: Erwin Cotton Mills

275465.title: Washington, DC
275465.description:
This category has web sites with information on airports serving Washington, DC.

There are no airports within the boundaries of the District of Columbia itself; all commercial and general aviation airports serving the metropolitan area are located in Maryland or Virginia. 275176.title: Software
275176.description: The Distribution-industry specific software area covers software companies and products of interest to distributors and wholesalers. Types of software found under this category include inventory management, order entry,  warehouse management, electronic data interchange (EDI), and the emerging area of electronic commerce and XML and BizTalk. The reason for distribution being a separate from general business or enterprise resource management (ERP) is that the distributor occupies a distinct place in, what is called, the extended supply chain, that reaches from manufacturer to the end-customer. Some business trends attempt to remove the distributor from the supply chain (a process called disintermediation). A distributor's choice of business management software is critical in streamlining business processes, increasing profitability, reducing transaction costs, enhancing customer service, maximizing inventory investment, and remaining competitive and a valuable contributor in the supply chain.

275813.title: Freight Forwarding
275813.description: Freight forwarders facilitate the movement of goods in international trade by playing an intermediary role between their clients and the companies who pick up, transport, and deliver goods to their destinations. Freight forwarders negotiate freight rates with transport providers. Considering cost, speed, and reliability, they recommend the best mode of transport to their customers. Once a plan has been approved, they work to make sure the goods are transported and delivered as agreed.   In carrying out their work, freight forwarders frequently provide associated services, such as customs services, NVOCC services, warehousing, and advice about risk management, financing, and methods of payment.   This category is for sites about the topic of freight forwarding, and for the sites of businesses whose primary business activity is freight forwarding.   A subcategory named for a specific country is for sites focused primarily on shipping goods from that country to places elsewhere.

275572.title: Shipbreaking
275572.description: Ship breaking, also known as ship recycling, disposal, or demolition, involves deconstructing vessels into saleable or conventionally disposable components.   Most ship breaking now is done in Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and China, with a small amount in Turkey. Most of these operations are technically unsophisticated, generally involving beaching the vessel under power, removing motors, electronics, and such, then cutting up the vessel's steel for scrap. Ship breaking is the source of millions of tons of steel each year.  Concerns have been raised about environmental and worker safety in ship breaking yards.

278674.title: Wholesale Trade
278674.description:
The Wholesale Trade category comprises establishments whose primary function is to purchase goods and merchandise from producers and manufacturers and sell those goods, generally without transformation, to re-sellers, often in bulk.

Sites not listed in this category:

  • Sites for entities involved in the transportation of goods are listed in Business: Transportation and Logistics
  • Entities whose primary function is to facilitate wholesale transactions across international borders are collected in Business: International Business and Trade: Import and Export

278676.title: Directories
278676.description:
Wholesale

The Wholesale Trade sector comprises establishments engaged in wholesaling merchandise, generally without transformation, and rendering services incidental to the sale of merchandise.
The wholesaling process is an intermediate step in the distribution of merchandise. Wholesalers are organised to sell or arrange the purchase of sale of (a) goods for resale (i.e. goods sold to other wholesalers or retailers), (b) capital or durable nonconsumer goods, and (c) raw and intermediate materials and supplies used in production.
Wholesale/ contains sites of companies of whose primary focus is to purchase goods and merchandise from producers and manufacturers and to sell them to re-sellers in bulk.
Business/Wholesale_Trade/ lists the sites of companies which concentrate to the definition (a) above.

Wholesale

The Wholesale Trade sector comprises establishments engaged in wholesaling merchandise, generally without transformation, and rendering services incidental to the sale of merchandise.
The wholesaling process is an intermediate step in the distribution of merchandise. Wholesalers are organised to sell or arrange the purchase of sale of (a) goods for resale (i.e. goods sold to other wholesalers or retailers), (b) capital or durable nonconsumer goods, and (c) raw and intermediate materials and supplies used in production.
Wholesale/ contains sites of companies of whose primary focus is to purchase goods and merchandise from producers and manufacturers and to sell them to re-sellers in bulk.
Business/Wholesale_Trade/ lists the sites of companies which concentrate to the definition (a) above.
